events.text: Former deputy director of the Chilean secret police Raúl Iturriaga is captured after having been on the run following a conviction for kidnapping.

main.desc: Chilean secret police under the Pinochet dictatorship (1973–1977)

events.text: The last vessels involved in Taurus 09, a Royal Navy training deployment covering 20,400 miles (32,800 km), returned to HMNB Devonport, England.
Widespread rioting erupts in Karachi, Pakistan, after the assassination of a local politician, leaving at least 85 dead and at least 17 billion Pakistani rupees (US$200 million) in damage.

main.desc: Demonstrations after the murder of Pakistani politician Raza Haider

events.text: A 6.1 magnitude earthquake kills at least 617 people and injures more than 2,400 in Yunnan, China.
The genocide of Yazidis by ISIL begins.

main.desc: 2014-2017 genocide campaign by the Islamic State

events.text: Two burka-clad men kill 29 people and injure more than 80 in a suicide attack on a Shia mosque in eastern Afghanistan.
A mass shooting occurred at a Walmart in El Paso, Texas, killing 23 people and injuring 22 others.
Six hundred protesters, including opposition leader Lyubov Sobol, are arrested in an election protest in Moscow, Russia.

main.desc: Russian political and public figure, lawyer (born 1987)

events.text: Twenty-three people are killed and 22 injured in a mass shooting at a Walmart in El Paso, Texas.
Major floods hit parts of Slovenia.
The trial against Gaius Verres for corruption is opened, with Marcus Tullius Cicero as prosecutor and renowned orator Quintus Hortensius as defending lawyer.

Goguryeo-Sui War: In response to a Goguryeo (Korean) incursion into Liaoxi, Emperor Wéndi of Sui orders his youngest son, Yang Liang (assisted by the co-prime minister Gao Jiong), to conquer Goguryeo during the Manchurian rainy season, with a Chinese army and navy.

main.desc: Series of failed invasions of Korea by Sui-dynasty China between 598 and 614

events.text: Second Barons' War: Royal troops led by Prince Edward defeated baronial forces under Simon de Montfort at the Battle of Evesham in Worcestershire, England.

links.t: Simon de Montfort, 6th Earl of Leicester

events.text: Second Barons' War: Battle of Evesham: The army of Prince Edward (the future king Edward I of England) defeats the forces of rebellious barons led by Simon de Montfort, 6th Earl of Leicester, killing de Montfort and many of his allies.

links.t: Simon de Montfort, 6th Earl of Leicester

events.text: The so-called Black Parliament at Scone tries William II de Soules and other nobles who had plotted against Robert I of Scotland and intended to place William on the Scottish throne.

main.desc: Castle owned by the Earl of Mansfield in Perth & Kinross, Scotland

events.text: First War of Scottish Independence: James Douglas leads a raid into Weardale and almost kills Edward III of England.
Hundred Years' War: A large-scale mounted raid by Anglo-Gascon forces began under the command of Edward the Black Prince.

Battle of Al Kasr al Kebir: The Moroccans defeat the Portuguese but both the Moroccan king Abd al-Malik and the Portuguese king Sebastian die. Ahmad al-Mansur follows Abd al-Malik as sultan of Morocco while the death of Sebastian leads to a succession crisis in Portugal.

Date traditionally ascribed to Dom Perignon's invention of champagne; it is not clear whether he actually invented champagne, however he has been credited as an innovator who developed the techniques used to perfect sparkling wine.
Great Peace of Montreal between New France and First Nations is signed.

main.desc: 1701 peace treaty between New France and First Nations

events.text: War of the Spanish Succession: A combined Anglo-Dutch fleet under the command of George Rooke and allied with Archduke Charles captured Gibraltar from Spain.
War of the Spanish Succession: Gibraltar is captured by an English and Dutch fleet, commanded by Admiral Sir George Rooke and allied with Archduke Charles.
Fourth Anglo-Dutch War, a fleet of six East India Company ships sets sail from Fort Marlborough to raid the Dutch VOC factories on the West coast of Sumatra including the major port of Padang.

main.desc: War between Great Britain and Dutch Republic, 1780–1784

events.text: Mount Asama (pictured) in Japan began a climactic eruption, which exacerbated the Great Tenmei famine and led to thousands of deaths.

main.desc: Volcano on the island of Honshū, Japan

events.text: Mount Asama erupts in Japan, killing about 1,400 people (Tenmei eruption). The eruption causes a famine, which results in an additional 20,000 deaths.

main.desc: Volcano on the island of Honshū, Japan

events.text: France: abolition of feudalism by the National Constituent Assembly.
A newly passed tariff act creates the Revenue Cutter Service (the forerunner of the United States Coast Guard).
The Treaty of Sistova is signed, ending the Ottoman–Habsburg wars.

main.desc: Treaty ending the Austro-Turkish War of 1787–91

events.text: French Revolutionary Wars: Commanded by Napoleon Bonaparte, the French Army of Italy decisively defeated Austrian forces led by Peter Vitus von Quosdanovich at the Battle of Lonato.
French Revolutionary Wars: Napoleon leads the French Army of Italy to victory in the Battle of Lonato.
War of 1812: The ultimately unsuccessful Siege of Fort Erie begins as British forces attempt to recapture the fort and drive American forces out of Canada.
The Saturday Evening Post is published for the first time as a weekly newspaper.
American surveyor James Thompson produced the first plat of Chicago for the Illinois and Michigan Canal Commissioners.
The Hinomaru is established as the official flag to be flown from Japanese ships.
In Brooklyn, a mob composed largely of Irish Americans attacked a group of African Americans in a riot.

main.desc: Borough and county in New York, US

events.text: Matica slovenská, Slovakia's public-law cultural and scientific institution focusing on topics around the Slovak nation, is established in Martin.

main.desc: Cultural institution based in Martin, Slovakia

events.text: American Indian Wars: While protecting a railroad survey party in Montana, the United States 7th Cavalry, under Lieutenant Colonel George Armstrong Custer clashes for the first time with the Cheyenne and Lakota people near the Tongue River; only one man on each side is killed.

main.desc: Frontier conflicts in the United States, 1609–1890s

events.text: Granny, a sea anemone, died in Edinburgh after nearly 60 years in captivity. Her death was reported in The Scotsman and The New York Times.
The Great Fire of Spokane, Washington destroys some 32 blocks of the city, prompting a mass rebuilding project.
Lizzie Borden's father and stepmother were found murdered in their home in Fall River, Massachusetts; Borden was later tried and acquitted for the murders.
The father and stepmother of Lizzie Borden are found murdered in their Fall River, Massachusetts home. She will be tried and acquitted for the crimes a year later.
World War I: Adhering to the terms of the Treaty of London, the United Kingdom declared war on Germany in response to the latter's invasion of Belgium.
World War I: In response to the German invasion of Belgium, Belgium and the British Empire declare war on Germany. The United States declares its neutrality.
World War I: The German 12th Army occupies Warsaw during the Gorlice–Tarnów Offensive and the Great Retreat of 1915.

main.desc: German army group on the Eastern Front of World War I

events.text: Bolshevik–Makhnovist conflict: Mikhail Frunze declares victory over the Makhnovshchina.

main.desc: 1920–21 political and military conflict in southern Ukraine

events.text: Enver Pasha dies in a skirmish between the Bolshevik Red Army and Basmachi troops, to whom he had defected earlier.
Diplomatic relations between Mexico and the Soviet Union are established.
Prime Minister of Greece Ioannis Metaxas suspends parliament and the Constitution and establishes the 4th of August Regime.

main.t: List of prime ministers of Greece

events.text: The Holocaust: A tip from a Dutch informer leads the Gestapo to a sealed-off area in an Amsterdam warehouse, where they find and arrest Jewish diarist Anne Frank, her family, and four others.

main.desc: Genocide of European Jews by Nazi Germany

events.text: Under the state of emergency law, the Finnish Parliament elects Marshal C. G. E. Mannerheim as the President of Finland to replace the resigned Risto Ryti.
An earthquake of magnitude 8.0 hits northern Dominican Republic. One hundred are killed and 20,000 are left homeless.

main.desc: 8.1 magnitude scale earthquake and tsunami near Dominican Republic

events.text: The Supreme Court of Japan is established.
Alfred C. Glassell Jr. caught a black marlin weighing 1,560 lb (710 kg) (pictured) off the coast of Peru, setting the record for the largest bony fish caught by hand.

Vietnam War: The National Security Agency falsely claimed that a U.S. Navy destroyer (pictured) was attacked a second time by North Vietnamese vessels in the Gulf of Tonkin, leading Congress to authorize the use of military force.
Civil rights movement: Civil rights workers Michael Schwerner, Andrew Goodman and James Chaney are found dead in Mississippi after disappearing on June 21.
Second Gulf of Tonkin Incident: U.S. destroyers USS Maddox and USS Turner Joy mistakenly report coming under attack in the Gulf of Tonkin.

main.desc: 1964 naval confrontation between North Vietnam and the United States

events.text: The Constitution of the Cook Islands comes into force, giving the Cook Islands self-governing status within New Zealand.

Vietnam War: At the apartment of French intermediary Jean Sainteny in Paris, American representative Henry Kissinger and North Vietnamese representative Xuân Thuỷ begin secret peace negotiations. The negotiations will eventually fail.
Ugandan President Idi Amin announces that Uganda is no longer responsible for the care of British subjects of Asian origin, beginning the expulsions of Ugandan Asians.
A bomb explodes in the Italicus Express train at San Benedetto Val di Sambro, Italy, killing 12 people and wounding 22.

main.desc: 1974 terror attack in San Benedetto Val di Sambro, Emilia-Romagna, Italy

events.text: The Japanese Red Army takes more than 50 hostages at the AIA Building housing several embassies in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. The hostages include the U.S. consul and the Swedish Chargé d'affaires. The gunmen win the release of five imprisoned comrades and fly with them to Libya.

links.t: History of Libya under Muammar Gaddafi

events.text: U.S. President Jimmy Carter signs legislation creating the United States Department of Energy.
Jean-Baptiste Ouédraogo, the president of Upper Volta, was ousted in a coup d'état led by Thomas Sankara.
Jean-Baptiste Ouédraogo, president of the military government of Upper Volta, is ousted from power in a coup d'état led by Captain Thomas Sankara.
The Republic of Upper Volta changes its name to Burkina Faso.

main.desc: Former country in West Africa (1958–1984); now Burkina Faso

events.text: The Ariane 3 rocket is launched for the first time, carrying the Eutelsat I F-2 and Télécom 1A satellites into geosynchronous transfer orbit.
The Federal Communications Commission rescinds the Fairness Doctrine which had required radio and television stations to give equal time to opposing views.
An explosion on the Greek cruise ship MTS Oceanos (pictured) ruptured its hull, causing it to sink off the east coast of South Africa, with all 571 people on board rescued.
Yugoslav Wars: The Croatian Army initiated Operation Storm, the last major battle of the Croatian War of Independence and the largest European land battle since the Second World War.

main.desc: 1991–2001 series of wars in the Balkans

events.text: Operation Storm, the last major battle of the Croatian War of Independence begins.

main.desc: 1995 military offensive and last major battle of the Croatian War of Independence

events.text: French supercentenarian Jeanne Calment died at the age of 122 years, 164 days, with the longest confirmed human lifespan in history.
Sri Lankan civil war: Seventeen employees of the French nongovernmental organization ACF International were massacred in Mutur.
A massacre is carried out by Sri Lankan government forces, killing 17 employees of the French INGO Action Against Hunger (known internationally as Action Contre la Faim, or ACF).

main.desc: Massacre of humanitarian workers in Muttur, Sri Lanka, 2006

events.text: An airport police officer discovered a suitcase containing approximately US$800,000 as it passed through security at Jorge Newbery Airfield in Buenos Aires, sparking an international scandal involving Venezuela and Argentina.

main.desc: Former airport police officer from Argentina

events.text: NASA's Phoenix Mars lander is launched.
Julieka Ivanna Dhu, an Aboriginal Australian woman, died in police custody after her deteriorating condition was mocked and ignored.

main.desc: One of the two categories of Indigenous Australians

events.text: Syrian civil war: The Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) expel the Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant (ISIL) from the Iraq–Syria border, concluding the second phase of the Deir ez-Zor campaign.
Crisis in Venezuela: Seven people are injured when two drones detonate explosives on Avenida Bolívar, Caracas while president Nicolás Maduro is giving a speech to the Venezuelan National Guard.

main.desc: Socioeconomic and political conjuncture in 21st century Venezuela

events.text: Nine people are killed and 26 injured in a shooting in Dayton, Ohio. This comes only 13 hours after another mass shooting in El Paso, Texas, where 23 people were killed.
A large explosion of ammonium nitrate stored at the Port of Beirut in Lebanon killed 218 people and caused US$15 billion in damage.
Beirut Port explosion: At least 220 people are killed and over 5,000 are wounded when 2,700 tons of ammonium nitrate explodes in Beirut, Lebanon.
Liu Xiu (pictured) proclaimed himself the monarch of the Han dynasty as Emperor Guangwu.

main.desc: Third decade of the first century AD

links.t: List of emperors of the Han dynasty

events.text: Guangwu claims the throne as Emperor of China, restoring the Han dynasty after the collapse of the short-lived Xin dynasty.

main.desc: Third decade of the first century AD

events.text: Fires resulting from the destruction of the Second Temple in Jerusalem are extinguished.
Battle of Maserfield: Penda of Mercia defeats and kills Oswald of Northumbria.

The last major Danish army to raid England for nearly a century is defeated at the Battle of Tettenhall by the allied forces of Mercia and Wessex, led by King Edward the Elder and Æthelred, Lord of the Mercians.
The Battle of Alhandic is fought between Ramiro II of León and Abd-ar-Rahman III at Zamora in the context of the Spanish Reconquista. The battle resulted in a victory for the Emirate of Córdoba.
Abbasid Caliph al-Muti' is forced to abdicate by his Turkic general Sabuktakin and succeeded by his son al-Ta'i'.
Byzantine–Norman wars: Italo-Normans begin a nearly-three-year siege of Bari.

main.desc: Series of Norman invasions of the Byzantine Empire between 1040 and 1189

events.text: Henry I was crowned King of England in Westminster Abbey.
Henry I is crowned King of England in Westminster Abbey.
Richard I of England defeats Saladin in the battle of Jaffa, which enables him to conclude a favourable treaty for the crusaders.
Spanish Reconquista: the forces of the Kingdom of Castile initiate the ultimately futile Siege of Algeciras against the Emirate of Granada.

First Scottish War of Independence: Sir John Stewart of Menteith, the pro-English Sheriff of Dumbarton, successfully manages to capture Sir William Wallace of Scotland, leading to Wallace's subsequent execution by hanging, evisceration, drawing and quartering, and beheading 18 days later.
The Battle of Otterburn, a border skirmish between the Scottish and the English in Northern England, is fought near Otterburn.
The Kingdom of Scotland captures Roxburgh, one of the last English strongholds in Scotland, following a siege.
Muscovite–Lithuanian Wars: The Grand Duchy of Lithuania achieved one of the greatest Lithuanian victories against the Tatars at the Battle of Kletsk.

main.desc: Series of wars between the Grand Duchy of Lithuania and the Grand Duchy of Moscow

events.text: The Grand Duchy of Lithuania defeats the Crimean Khanate in the Battle of Kletsk.
Sir Humphrey Gilbert establishes the first English colony in North America, at what is now St. John's, Newfoundland and Labrador.
Scottish nobleman John Ruthven, 3rd Earl of Gowrie, was killed during what was most likely a failed attempt to kidnap King James VI.
The Gowrie Conspiracy against King James VI of Scotland (later to become King James I of England) takes place at Gowrie House (Perth, Scotland).

The Mayflower departs from Southampton, England, carrying would-be settlers, on its first attempt to reach North America; it is forced to dock in Dartmouth when its companion ship, the Speedwell, springs a leak.
Beaver Wars: Aggravated by increased French incursions into their territory, a large force of Mohawk warriors substantially destroyed the settlement of Lachine in present-day Quebec.
Beaver Wars: Fifteen hundred Iroquois attack Lachine in New France.
Austro-Turkish War: The Ottoman army were defeated in their attempt to capture the Habsburg-controlled Petrovaradin Fortress despite having twice the number of soldiers.

main.desc: War between the Habsburg monarchy and the Ottoman Empire in the 18th century

events.text: Austro-Turkish War (1716–1718):The Austrians defeat the Ottomans in the Battle of Petrovaradin. One-fifth of a Turkish army and the Grand Vizier are killed.

main.desc: War between the Habsburg monarchy and the Ottoman Empire in the 18th century

events.text: Freedom of the press: New York Weekly Journal writer John Peter Zenger is acquitted of seditious libel against the royal governor of New York, on the basis that what he had published was true.

main.desc: Freedom of communication and expression through various media

events.text: Pontiac's War: Battle of Bushy Run: British forces led by Henry Bouquet defeat Chief Pontiac's Indians at Bushy Run.

main.desc: 1763 conflict by indigenous Native Americans against the British in Canada

links.t: Native Americans in the United States

events.text: An earthquake in the Sea of Marmara and Gallipoli (present-day Turkey) along the North Anatolian Fault kills at least 5,000 people.

main.desc: Earthquake with epicenter in the western part of the Sea of Marmara

events.text: Russia, Prussia and Habsburg Austria began the First Partition of Poland, with the primary motive to restore the regional balance of power in Eastern Europe.

First Partition of Poland: The representatives of Austria, Prussia, and Russia sign three bilateral conventions condemning the "anarchy" of the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth and imputing to the three powers "ancient and legitimate rights" to the territories of the Commonwealth. The conventions allow each of the three great powers to annex a part of the Commonwealth, which they proceed to do over the course of the following two months.
British and Dutch ships engage in the second Battle of Dogger Bank.

main.desc: 1781 battle of the Fourth Anglo-Dutch War

events.text: The Battle of Castiglione in Napoleon's first Italian campaigns of the French Revolutionary Wars results in a French victory.

main.desc: 1796 battle during the War of the First Coalition

links.t: Italian campaigns of the French Revolutionary Wars

events.text: Sir John Barrow, secretary at the Admiralty, rejected a proposal to use Francis Ronalds's electrical telegraph, deeming it "wholly unnecessary".

main.desc: English geographer, linguist, and civil servant (1764–1848)

events.text: The British Admiralty dismisses Francis Ronalds's new invention of the first working electric telegraph as "wholly unnecessary", preferring to continue using the semaphore.
Greek War of Independence: Konstantinos Kanaris leads a Greek fleet to victory against Ottoman and Egyptian naval forces in the Battle of Samos.

main.desc: Greek rebellion against the Ottoman Empire (1821–1829)

events.text: Cyrus West Field and others complete the first transatlantic telegraph cable after several unsuccessful attempts. It will operate for less than a month.
Charles XV of Sweden–Norway is crowned king of Norway in Trondheim.

main.desc: King of Sweden and Norway from 1859 to 1872

events.text: American Civil War: In order to help pay for the war effort, the United States government levies the first income tax as part of the Revenue Act of 1861 (3% of all incomes over US$800; rescinded in 1872).

links.t: Federal government of the United States

events.text: The United States Army abolishes flogging.

main.desc: Land service branch of the U.S. military

events.text: American Civil War: Battle of Baton Rouge: Along the Mississippi River near Baton Rouge, Louisiana, Confederate troops attempt to take the city, but are driven back by fire from Union gunboats.

main.desc: Battle of the American Civil War

events.text: American Civil War: The Battle of Mobile Bay begins at Mobile Bay near Mobile, Alabama, Admiral David Farragut leads a Union flotilla through Confederate defenses and seals one of the last major Southern ports.

main.desc: Naval battle of the American Civil War

events.text: Japan launches its postal savings system, modeled after a similar system in the United Kingdom.

main.desc: Banking services offered by a postal system

events.text: Standard Oil Company of New Jersey, today known as ExxonMobil, is established officially. The company would later grow to become the holder of all Standard Oil companies and the entity at the center of the breakup of Standard Oil.

links.t: Standard Oil Co. of New Jersey v. United States

events.text: The cornerstone for the Statue of Liberty is laid on Bedloe's Island (now Liberty Island) in New York Harbor.

main.desc: Colossal sculpture in New York Harbor

events.text: Bertha Benz made the first long-distance automobile trip, driving 106 km (66 mi) from Mannheim to Pforzheim, Germany, in a Benz Patent-Motorwagen.

main.desc: German automobile pioneer, with husband Carl Benz

events.text: Bertha Benz drives from Mannheim to Pforzheim and back in the first long distance automobile trip, commemorated as the Bertha Benz Memorial Route since 2008.

main.desc: German automobile pioneer, with husband Carl Benz

events.text: Peter O'Connor sets the first World Athletics recognised long jump world record of 24 ft 11.75 in (7.6137 m), a record that would stand for 20 years.

links.t: List of world records in athletics

events.text: Persian Constitutional Revolution: Mozaffar ad-Din Shah Qajar, King of Iran, agrees to convert the government to a constitutional monarchy.
World War I: The German minelayer SS Königin Luise lays a minefield about 40 miles (64 km) off the Thames Estuary (Lowestoft). She is intercepted and sunk by the British light-cruiser HMS Amphion.

World War I: The guns of Point Nepean fort at Port Phillip Heads in Victoria (Australia) fire across the bows of the Norddeutscher Lloyd steamer SS Pfalz which is attempting to leave the Port of Melbourne in ignorance of the declaration of war and she is detained; this is said to be the first Allied shot of the War.

main.desc: German cargo steamship, operational from 1913 to her wreckage in 1937

events.text: In Cleveland, Ohio, the first electric traffic light is installed.
First World War: The British Empire's Sinai and Palestine campaign began with a victory at the Battle of Romani.

World War I: Battle of Romani: Allied forces, under the command of Archibald Murray, defeat an attacking Ottoman army under the command of Friedrich Freiherr Kress von Kressenstein, securing the Suez Canal and beginning the Ottoman retreat from the Sinai Peninsula.

main.desc: 1916 World War I attack on Suez Canal

events.text: Plaid Cymru is formed with the aim of disseminating knowledge of the Welsh language that is at the time in danger of dying out.
Harry Houdini performs his greatest feat, spending 91 minutes underwater in a sealed tank before escaping.
Judge and Nazi Party member Werner Best drafts the Boxheim Documents, which described a violent takeover of the government by the NSDAP.
The Thirteen Roses: Thirteen female members of the Unified Socialist Youth are executed by Francoist forces in Madrid, Spain.

main.desc: Group of 13 young women executed in Francoist Spain

events.text: World War II: The Soviet Union formally annexes Latvia.

World War II: At least 1,104 Japanese POWs in Australia attempt to escape from a camp at Cowra, New South Wales; 545 temporarily succeed but are later either killed, commit suicide, or are recaptured.
World War II: Polish insurgents liberate a German labor camp (Gęsiówka) in Warsaw, freeing 348 Jewish prisoners.
World War II: The Nazis begin a week-long massacre of between 40,000 and 50,000 civilians and prisoners of war in Wola, Poland.

main.desc: 1944 extermination of civilians by Nazi forces in Wola, Warsaw, Poland

events.text: An earthquake registering 6.4 Ms struck near Ambato, Ecuador, killing 5,050 people.
In Ecuador, an earthquake destroys 50 towns and kills more than 6,000.
In Montana, 12 smokejumper firefighters and a US Forest Service fire guard are killed in the Mann Gulch Fire.
American Bandstand, a show dedicated to the teenage "baby-boomers" by playing the songs and showing popular dances of the time, debuts on the ABC television network.
Burkina Faso, then known as Upper Volta, becomes independent from France.
American actress and model Marilyn Monroe was found dead of a barbiturate overdose in her home in Brentwood, Los Angeles.
Apartheid: Nelson Mandela is jailed. He would not be released until 1990.

main.desc: South African system of racial segregation

events.text: American actress Marilyn Monroe is found dead at her home from a drug overdose.
Cold War: The United States, the United Kingdom, and the Soviet Union sign the Partial Nuclear Test Ban Treaty.

main.desc: 1947–1991 geopolitical rivalry between US and USSR

events.text: Vietnam War: Operation Pierce Arrow: American aircraft from carriers USS Ticonderoga and USS Constellation bomb North Vietnam in retaliation for strikes against U.S. destroyers in the Gulf of Tonkin.
The Indo-Pakistani war of 1965 begins as Pakistani soldiers cross the Line of Control dressed as locals.

A group of red guards at Experimental High in Beijing, including Deng Rong and Liu Pingping, daughters of Deng Xiaoping and Liu Shaoqi respectively, beat the deputy vice principal, Bian Zhongyun, to death with sticks after accusing her of counter-revolutionary revisionism, producing one of the first fatalities of the Cultural Revolution.

links.t: Experimental High School Attached to Beijing Normal University

events.text: Police raided a screening of the film Lonesome Cowboys in Atlanta, Georgia, leading to the creation of a Gay Liberation Front in that city.

main.desc: 1969 anti-LGBT raid in Atlanta, Georgia, US

events.text: The Lonesome Cowboys police raid occurs in Atlanta, Georgia, leading to the creation of the Georgia Gay Liberation Front.

main.desc: 1969 anti-LGBT raid in Atlanta, Georgia, US

events.text: The first Pacific Islands Forum (then known as the "South Pacific Forum") is held in Wellington, New Zealand, with the aim of enhancing cooperation between the independent countries of the Pacific Ocean.

main.desc: Intergovernmental organisation of island nations in the Pacific Ocean

events.text: Due to an athletics scandal, the National Collegiate Athletic Association applied the death penalty to the basketball program at the University of Southwestern Louisiana.

main.t: University of Southwestern Louisiana basketball scandal

events.text: Mars 6 is launched from the USSR.

Watergate scandal: President Richard Nixon, under orders of the US Supreme Court, releases the "Smoking Gun" tape, recorded on June 23, 1972, clearly revealing his actions in covering up and interfering investigations into the break-in. His political support vanishes completely.

links.t: Supreme Court of the United States

events.text: In Afghanistan, Maoists undertake the Bala Hissar uprising against the Leninist government.
U.S. president Ronald Reagan fired the 11,345 striking members of the Professional Air Traffic Controllers Organization en masse.

main.desc: President of the United States from 1981 to 1989

events.text: President Ronald Reagan fires 11,359 striking air-traffic controllers who ignored his order for them to return to work.

main.desc: President of the United States from 1981 to 1989

events.text: A Biman Bangladesh Airlines aircraft crashed while attempting to land in Dhaka, killing 49 people in the deadliest aviation accident in Bangladeshi history.
A Biman Bangladesh Airlines Fokker F27 Friendship crashes on approach to Zia International Airport, in Dhaka, Bangladesh, killing all 49 people on board.
Wizards of the Coast released Magic: The Gathering, the first trading card game.
Yugoslav Wars: The city of Knin, Croatia, a significant Serb stronghold, is taken by Croatian forces during Operation Storm. The date is celebrated in Croatia as Victory Day.

main.desc: 1991–2001 series of wars in the Balkans

events.text: A car bomb explodes in the Indonesian capital of Jakarta outside the Marriott Hotel killing 12 and injuring 150.
The New England Revolution win the 2008 North American SuperLiga final against the Houston Dynamo.

main.desc: American soccer club in Greater Boston

events.text: The Copiapó mining accident occurs, trapping 33 Chilean miners approximately 2,300 ft (700 m) below the ground for 69 days.

main.desc: Cave-in and miner rescue in Atacama Region, Chile

events.text: Ten members of International Assistance Mission Nuristan Eye Camp team are killed by persons unknown in Kuran wa Munjan District of Badakhshan Province, Afghanistan.

main.desc: Christian development non-governmental organization operating in Afghanistan

events.text: NASA launched the Juno probe to Jupiter as part of the New Frontiers program.

main.desc: Second NASA orbiter mission to Jupiter (2011–Present)

events.text: Radio Network House (pictured), damaged in the 2011 Christchurch earthquake, becomes the first building to be demolished by implosion in New Zealand.
An American white supremacist carried out a mass shooting at a Sikh temple in Oak Creek, Wisconsin, killing six people and wounding four others.

main.desc: Belief in the superiority of white people

events.text: Radio Network House, damaged in the 2011 Christchurch earthquake, becomes the first building to be demolished by implosion in New Zealand.
The Wisconsin Sikh temple shooting took place in Oak Creek, Wisconsin, killing six victims; the perpetrator committed suicide after being wounded by police.

United States Environmental Protection Agency personnel accidentally caused a spillage (aftermath pictured) of 3 million gallons (11 million litres) of mine waste water and tailings trapped inside the Gold King Mine near Silverton, Colorado.

links.t: 2015 Gold King Mine waste water spill

events.text: The Environmental Protection Agency at Gold King Mine waste water spill releases three million gallons of heavy metal toxin tailings and waste water into the Animas River in Colorado.

main.t: 2015 Gold King Mine waste water spill

events.text: The revocation of the special status of Jammu and Kashmir (state) occurred and the state was bifurcated into two union territories (Jammu and Kashmir (union territory) and Ladakh).

main.t: Revocation of the special status of Jammu and Kashmir

events.text: Australia's second most populous state Victoria enters its sixth COVID-19 lockdown, enacting stage four restrictions statewide in reaction to six new COVID-19 cases recorded that morning.

Following the non-cooperation movement against the government of Bangladesh, Bangladeshi prime minister Sheikh Hasina resigns and flees the country, ending her rule of 15 consecutive years and a total of almost two decades. The date is also known as 36 July.

main.desc: Mass uprising against the government of Bangladesh

events.text: Pope Sixtus II is arrested while celebrating mass and then beheaded with several of his deacons.

main.desc: Head of the Catholic Church from 257 to 258

events.text: Second Fitna: Pro-Alid forces defeated the Umayyad Caliphate at the Battle of Khazir, allowing them to take control of Mosul in present-day Iraq.
The Umayyad forces suffer a decisive defeat against the pro-Alid forces under Ibrahim ibn al-Ashtar in the battle of Khazir.
Antipope Constantine II is deposed and blinded by the Lombard troops of primicerius Christopher.
The Republic of Pisa is defeated in the Battle of Meloria by the Republic of Genoa, thus losing its naval dominance in the Mediterranean.
Bogotá, Colombia, is founded by Gonzalo Jiménez de Quesada.

main.desc: Capital and largest city of Colombia

events.text: Toyotomi Hideyoshi is officially appointed kampaku (Imperial Regent).

main.desc: Military ruler of Japan from 1585 to 1598

main.t: Embassy of the United States, Havana
main.desc: American diplomatic mission in the capital of Cuba

events.text: The collapse of the Ponte Morandi bridge in Genoa, Italy, left 16 people injured and 43 people killed.
A magnitude 7.2 earthquake struck in Haiti, killing at least 2,248 people and causing $1.5 billion in damages and economic loss.
A magnitude 7.2 earthquake strikes southwestern Haiti, killing at least 2,248 people and causing a humanitarian crisis.
An explosion destroys a market in Armenia, killing six people and injuring dozens.
Former U.S. president Donald Trump is charged in Georgia along with 18 others in attempting to overturn the results of the 2020 election in that state, his fourth indictment of 2023.

main.desc: President of the United States (2017–2021; since 2025)

events.text: Arab–Byzantine wars: The Battle of Yarmouk between the Byzantine Empire and the Rashidun Caliphate begins.

main.desc: Series of wars between the 7th and 11th centuries

events.text: Arab–Byzantine wars: Maslama ibn Abd al-Malik begins the Second Arab Siege of Constantinople, which will last for nearly a year.

main.desc: 8th century Umayyad prince and military leader

events.text: Forces of the Umayyad Caliphate abandoned a year-long siege of Constantinople, ending their goal of conquering the Byzantine Empire.

Arab–Byzantine wars: The Arabs abandon the Second Arab Siege of Constantinople due to failure to secure enough supplies, defeat of their relief army by the Byzantines and an outbreak of plague in the camp.

Carloman, mayor of the palace of Austrasia, renounces his position as majordomo and retires to a monastery near Rome. His brother, Pepin the Short, becomes the sole ruler (de facto) of the Frankish Kingdom.
The Battle of Roncevaux Pass takes place between the army of Charlemagne and a Basque army.
Noble Erchana of Dahauua grants the Bavarian town of Dachau to the Diocese of Freising.
The Arabs under Caliph al-Mu'tasim storm and sack the city of Amorium, killing half the population and enslaving the other.
The Saracens conquer and destroy Taranto.

main.desc: Archaic term for Arabs and later for all Muslims

events.text: Holy Roman Emperor Otto II is defeated by the Saracens in the Battle of Capo Colonna, in Calabria.

main.desc: Ruler of the Holy Roman Empire from 800 to 1806

events.text: Byzantine general Eustathios Daphnomeles captured and blinded Ibatzes of Bulgaria by means of a ruse, ending the last resistance against Emperor Basil II's conquest of Bulgaria.
Byzantine general Eustathios Daphnomeles blinds and captures Ibatzes of Bulgaria by a ruse, thereby ending Bulgarian resistance against Emperor Basil II's conquest of Bulgaria.
Upon the death of his uncle Stephen I, Peter (depicted) became the second king of Hungary.

main.desc: King of Hungary from 1000/1001 to 1038; Catholic saint

events.text: King Stephen I, the first king of Hungary, dies; his nephew, Peter Orseolo, succeeds him.

main.desc: King of Hungary from 1000/1001 to 1038; Catholic saint

events.text: King Macbeth of Scotland is killed at the Battle of Lumphanan by the forces of Máel Coluim mac Donnchada.
The Pavian-born Benedictine Lanfranc is appointed as the new Archbishop of Canterbury in England.
Starting date of the First Crusade as set by Pope Urban II.

main.desc: 1096–1099 Christian re-conquest of the Holy Land

events.text: Seljuk Sultan Ghiyath ad-Din Mas'ud enters Baghdad after he besieged it for fifty days and the flight of Abbasid caliph al-Rashid Billah the day before.
The cave city of Vardzia is consecrated by Queen Tamar of Georgia.
Albigensian Crusade: The Cathar stronghold of Carcassonne falls to the crusaders.

main.desc: 13th-century crusade against Catharism in southern France

events.text: The Livonian Brothers of the Sword, a Catholic military order, occupy Tarbatu (today Tartu) as part of the Livonian Crusade.
Spanish Reconquista: The Battle of the Puig between the Moorish forces of Taifa of Valencia against the Crown of Aragon culminates in an Aragonese victory.
The foundation stone of Cologne Cathedral, built to house the relics of the Three Wise Men, is laid. (Construction is eventually completed in 1880.)

main.desc: First stone set in construction of a masonry foundation

events.text: Michael VIII Palaiologos was crowned Byzantine emperor in Constantinople.
Michael VIII Palaiologos leads a triumphal procession into Constantinople following its recapture and is crowned Byzantine emperor.
Mongol invasions of Japan: The Mongolian fleet of Kublai Khan is destroyed by a "divine wind" for the second time in the Battle of Kōan.

The city of Rhodes surrenders to the forces of the Knights of St. John, completing their conquest of Rhodes. The knights establish their headquarters on the island and rename themselves the Knights of Rhodes.
Francesco Sforza, lord of Milan, conquers Lucca.

main.desc: Italian condottiero and Sforza dynasty founder (1401–1466)

events.text: The Empire of Trebizond surrenders to the forces of Sultan Mehmed II. This is regarded by some historians as the real end of the Byzantine Empire. Emperor David of Trebizond is exiled and later murdered.
Pope Sixtus IV consecrates the Sistine Chapel.

main.desc: Head of the Catholic Church from 1471 to 1484

events.text: Afonso de Albuquerque of Portugal conquers Malacca, the capital of the Malacca Sultanate.
Seven Portuguese armed vessels led by Fernão Pires de Andrade meet Chinese officials at the Pearl River estuary.
Panama City, Panama is founded.

main.desc: Capital and largest city of the Republic of Panama

events.text: Ignatius of Loyola and six classmates take initial vows, leading to the creation of the Society of Jesus in September 1540.

main.desc: Basque Spaniard Catholic priest and theologian (1491–1556)

events.text: Asunción, Paraguay is founded.

main.desc: Capital and most populous city of Paraguay

events.text: Arequipa, Peru is founded.
Jesuit priest Francis Xavier comes ashore at Kagoshima (Traditional Japanese date: 22 July 1549).

main.desc: Male religious congregation of the Catholic Church

events.text: Imjin War: At the Battle of Hansan Island, the Korean Navy, led by Yi Sun-sin, Yi Ŏkki, and Wŏn Kyun, decisively defeats the Japanese Navy, led by Wakisaka Yasuharu.
Nine Years' War: Battle of Curlew Pass: Irish forces led by Hugh Roe O'Donnell successfully ambush English forces, led by Sir Conyers Clifford, sent to relieve Collooney Castle.
A Royalist army under the Marquess of Montrose defeats a Covenanter army in the battle of Kilsyth.
Emperor Leopold I and French king Louis XIV agree to an armistice in the truce of Ratisbon.
French forces end the bombardment of Brussels.

main.desc: 1695 battle of the Nine Years' War

events.text: Seven Years' War: Battle of Liegnitz: Frederick the Great's victory over the Austrians under Ernst Gideon von Laudon.
War of 1812: Potawatomi warriors ambushed a United States Army convoy after it had evacuated Fort Dearborn, in present-day Chicago, and razed the fort.
War of 1812: British forces launch a costly and unsuccessful night attack against American defenders during the siege of Fort Erie.
The Marquis de Lafayette, the last surviving French general of the American Revolutionary War, arrives in New York and begins a tour of 24 states.

links.t: Visit of the Marquis de Lafayette to the United States

events.text: The Cathedral of Our Lady of Peace in Honolulu, Hawaii is dedicated. Now the cathedral of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Honolulu, it is the oldest Roman Catholic cathedral in continuous use in the United States.

main.t: Cathedral Basilica of Our Lady of Peace
main.desc: Historic Roman Catholic church in Hawaii, United States

events.text: Tivoli Gardens, one of the oldest still intact amusement parks in the world, opens in Copenhagen, Denmark.

main.desc: Amusement park and pleasure garden in Copenhagen, Denmark

events.text: The Anglo-Satsuma War begins between the Satsuma Domain of Japan and the United Kingdom (Traditional Japanese date: July 2, 1863).

main.desc: 1863 naval battle between Britain and the Satsuma Domain of Japan

events.text: Start of the second part of the Montceau-les-Mines troubles by the Black Band, groups of anarchist miners.
Ibadan area becomes a British Protectorate after a treaty was signed by Fijabi, the Baale of Ibadan, with the British acting Governor of Lagos, George C. Denton.

main.desc: Capital city of Oyo State, Nigeria

events.text: Fratton Park football ground in Portsmouth, England is officially first opened.

main.desc: Association football ground in Portsmouth, England

events.text: Ordination in Constantinople of Fr. Raphael Morgan, the first African-American Orthodox priest, "Priest-Apostolic" to America and the West Indies.
A military coup against the government of Dimitrios Rallis began in the neighbourhood of Goudi in Athens, Greece.
A servant of American architect, Frank Lloyd Wright, sets fire to the living quarters of Wright's Wisconsin home, Taliesin, and murders seven people there.

main.desc: Person who designs buildings and oversees construction

events.text: The Panama Canal opens to traffic with the transit of the cargo ship SS Ancon.
World War I: The First Russian Army, led by Paul von Rennenkampf, enters East Prussia.
World War I: Beginning of the Battle of Cer, the first Allied victory of World War I.

main.desc: Battle fought between Austria-Hungary and Serbia in August 1914

events.text: A story in the New York World newspaper reveals that the Imperial German government had purchased excess phenol from Thomas Edison that could be used to make explosives for the war effort and diverted it to Bayer for aspirin production.

main.desc: German WWI plot to divert US phenol

events.text: Polish–Soviet War: Battle of Warsaw, so-called Miracle at the Vistula.
Will Rogers and Wiley Post are killed after their aircraft develops engine problems during takeoff in Barrow, Alaska.

main.desc: Cherokee humorist and entertainer from Indian Territory, U.S. (1879–1935)

events.text: Twenty-six Junkers Ju 87 bombers commanded by Walter Sigel meet unexpected ground fog during a dive-bombing demonstration for Luftwaffe generals at Neuhammer. Thirteen of them crash and burn.

main.desc: 1935 dive bomber aircraft family by Junkers

events.text: The Wizard of Oz premieres at Grauman's Chinese Theater in Los Angeles, California.

main.desc: 1939 film based on the book by L. Frank Baum

events.text: An Italian submarine torpedoes and sinks the Greek cruiser Elli at Tinos harbor during peacetime, marking the most serious Italian provocation prior to the outbreak of the Greco-Italian War in October.
Decree for the mass expulsion of ethnic Germans from Crimea issued by the Soviet government.

main.desc: Soviet forced displacement of ethnic Germans

events.text: Josef Jakobs, a German spy, became the last person executed at the Tower of London.
Corporal Josef Jakobs is executed by firing squad for espionage at the Tower of London at 07:12, making him the last person to be executed at the Tower.
World War II: The tanker SS Ohio reached Malta as part of an operation to deliver much-needed supplies during the siege of Malta.
World War II: Operation Pedestal: The oil tanker SS Ohio reaches the island of Malta barely afloat carrying vital fuel supplies for the island's defenses.
World War II: Battle of Trahili: Superior German forces surround Cretan partisans, who manage to escape against all odds.

main.desc: 1943 battle during the German occupation of Crete in World War II

events.text: World War II: Allied forces began Operation Dragoon, their invasion of southern France.
World War II: Operation Dragoon: Allied forces land in southern France.
Emperor Hirohito broadcasts his declaration of surrender following the effective surrender of Japan in World War II; Korea gains independence from the Empire of Japan.
Jawaharlal Nehru (pictured) took office as the first prime minister of India, a post he held for 16 years.

main.desc: Prime Minister of India from 1947 to 1964

events.text: India gains independence from British rule after nearly 190 years of British company and crown rule and joins the Commonwealth of Nations.
Founder of Pakistan Muhammad Ali Jinnah is sworn in as first Governor-General of Pakistan in Karachi.
The Republic of Korea was established with Syngman Rhee as its first president.
The First Republic of Korea (South Korea) is established in the southern half of the peninsula.

main.desc: Government of South Korea from 1948 to 1960

events.text: Measuring Mw 8.6, the largest earthquake on land occurs in the Assam-Tibet-Myanmar border, killing 4,800.
A flash flood devastates the town of Lynmouth, England, killing 34 people.

main.desc: 1952 natural disaster in the county of Devon, England

events.text: Alfredo Stroessner begins his dictatorship in Paraguay.
American Airlines Flight 514, a Boeing 707, crashes near the Calverton Executive Airpark in Calverton, New York, killing all five people on board.

main.desc: 1959 aviation accident on Long Island, New York

events.text: Republic of the Congo (Brazzaville) becomes independent from France.
Border guard Conrad Schumann flees from East Germany while on duty guarding the construction of the Berlin Wall.
James Joseph Dresnok defects to North Korea after running across the Korean Demilitarized Zone. Dresnok died in 2016.
President Fulbert Youlou was overthrown in the Republic of Congo, after a three-day uprising in the capital.
Execution of Henry John Burnett, the last man to be hanged in Scotland.

main.desc: Scottish convicted murderer; last person to be executed by hanging in Scotland (1963)

events.text: President Fulbert Youlou is overthrown in the Republic of the Congo, after a three-day uprising in the capital.
The Beatles play to nearly 60,000 fans at Shea Stadium in New York City, an event later regarded as the birth of stadium rock.
The Woodstock Music & Art Fair opens in Bethel, New York, featuring some of the top rock musicians of the era.

main.desc: 1969 music festival in Bethel, New York, US

events.text: Patricia Palinkas becomes the first woman to play professionally in an American football game.
President Richard Nixon completes the break from the gold standard by ending convertibility of the United States dollar into gold by foreign investors.

main.desc: President of the United States from 1969 to 1974

events.text: Bahrain gains independence from the United Kingdom.
Vietnam War: The US Air Force bombing of Cambodia ends.
Yuk Young-soo, First Lady of South Korea, is killed during an apparent assassination attempt upon President Park Chung Hee.

main.desc: First Lady of South Korea from 1962 to 1974

events.text: Bangladeshi leader Sheikh Mujibur Rahman is killed along with most members of his family during a military coup.
Takeo Miki makes the first official pilgrimage to Yasukuni Shrine by an incumbent prime minister on the anniversary of the end of World War II.

main.desc: Prime Minister of Japan from 1974 to 1976

events.text: SAETA Flight 011 crashes into the Chimborazo volcano in Ecuador, killing all 59 people on board; the wreckage is not discovered until 2002.
Big Ear, a radio telescope at Ohio State University, received a strong, apparently extraterrestrial radio signal that became known as the Wow! signal (printout pictured).

main.desc: Kraus-type radio telescope in Ohio from 1963–98

events.text: The Big Ear, a radio telescope operated by Ohio State University as part of the SETI project, receives a radio signal from deep space; the event is named the "Wow! signal" from the notation made by a volunteer on the project.

main.desc: Kraus-type radio telescope in Ohio from 1963–98

events.text: The Kurdistan Workers' Party in Turkey starts a campaign of armed attacks upon the Turkish Armed Forces with an attack on police and gendarmerie bases in Şemdinli and Eruh.
Signing of the Assam Accord, an agreement between representatives of the Government of India and the leaders of the Assam Movement to end the movement.

main.desc: 1985 agreement between the Indian government and the Assam Movement

events.text: China Eastern Airlines Flight 5510 crashes after takeoff from Shanghai Hongqiao International Airport, killing 34 of the 40 people on board.
In South Carolina, Shannon Faulkner becomes the first female cadet matriculated at The Citadel (she drops out less than a week later).
Tomiichi Murayama, Prime Minister of Japan, releases the Murayama Statement, which formally expresses remorse for Japanese war crimes committed during World War II.

main.desc: Prime Minister of Japan from 1994 to 1996

events.text: The Troubles: A car bomb attack carried out by the Real Irish Republican Army killed 29 people and injured approximately 220 others in Omagh, Northern Ireland.
Northern Ireland: Omagh bombing takes place; 29 people (including a woman pregnant with twins) killed and some 220 others injured.
Apple introduces the iMac computer.
Beni Ounif massacre in Algeria: Some 29 people are killed at a false roadblock near the Moroccan border, leading to temporary tensions with Morocco.

main.desc: Commune and town in Béchar Province, Algeria

events.text: The Helsinki Agreement between the Free Aceh Movement and the Government of Indonesia was signed, ending more than 28 years of fighting.
Israel's unilateral disengagement plan to evict all Israelis from the Gaza Strip and from four settlements in the northern West Bank begins.

main.t: Israeli disengagement from the Gaza Strip

events.text: The Helsinki Agreement between the Free Aceh Movement and the Government of Indonesia is signed, ending almost three decades of fighting.
An 8.0-magnitude earthquake off the Pacific coast devastates Ica and various regions of Peru, killing 514 and injuring 1,090.

main.desc: Extreme earthquake and tsunami off the coast of Peru

events.text: At least 27 people are killed and 226 injured in an explosion in southern Beirut near a complex used by Lebanon's militant group Hezbollah in Lebanon. A previously unknown Syrian Sunni group claims responsibility in an online video.
The Smithsonian announces the discovery of the olinguito, the first new carnivorous species found in the Americas in 35 years.

main.desc: US group of museums and research centers

events.text: North Korea moves its clock back half an hour to introduce Pyongyang Time, 81⁄2 hours ahead of UTC.
Russia begins production on the Sputnik V COVID-19 vaccine.
Kabul falls into the hands of the Taliban as Ashraf Ghani flees Afghanistan along with local residents and foreign nationals, effectively reestablishing the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan.

main.desc: Capital and the largest city of Afghanistan

events.text: US president Donald Trump meets with Russian president Vladimir Putin in Alaska, the first such summit since the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine.

main.desc: President of the United States (2017–2021; since 2025)

events.text: Wang Mang consolidates his power in China and is declared marshal of state. Emperor Ai of Han, who died the previous day, had no heirs.

main.desc: Emperor of the Xin dynasty of China from 9 to 23

events.text: Start of the four-day Battle of al-Mada'in, between the Hamdanids of Mosul and the Baridis of Basra over control of the Abbasid capital, Baghdad.

main.desc: Battle for control of Baghdad in 942

events.text: Nikephoros II Phokas is crowned emperor of the Byzantine Empire, swearing to protect the two sons of the previous emperor Romanos II, who are already crowned co-emperors.
Nikephoros II Phokas captures the city of Tarsus, finalising the Byzantine conquest of Cilicia.
The House of Gonzaga seizes power in the Duchy of Mantua, and will rule until 1708.

main.desc: Italian royal family that ruled parts of Northern Italy

events.text: War of the League of Cambrai: English and Imperial forces defeated French cavalry, forcing them to retreat.

main.t: War of the League of Cambrai
main.desc: Fourth & Fifth phase of the Italian Wars (1508–1516)

events.text: Battle of the Spurs (Battle of Guinegate): King Henry VIII of England and his Imperial allies defeat French forces who are then forced to retreat.

main.desc: 1513 battle of the War of the League of Cambrai

events.text: Rabbi Moses Isserles issues his ruling in the Bragadin-Giustiniani dispute, one of the earliest instances of a copyright suit over any book.
The Principality of Transylvania is established after John II Zápolya renounces his claim as King of Hungary in the Treaty of Speyer.
Battle of Plymouth: Inconclusive naval action between the fleets of Michiel de Ruyter and George Ayscue in the First Anglo-Dutch War.

main.desc: 1652 naval battle of the Anglo-Dutch War

events.text: Great Turkish War: An imperial coalition army under Charles of Lorraine defeats the Ottoman army that had been besieging Esztergom.

main.desc: Conflicts between Ottomans and Holy League (1683–1699)

events.text: Austro-Turkish War (1716–1718): An imperial coalition army under Prince Eugene of Savoy defeats an Ottoman army under Haji Halil Pasha, leading to the surrender of the Ottoman garrison of Belgrade a few days later.

main.desc: War between the Habsburg monarchy and the Ottoman Empire in the 18th century

events.text: American Revolutionary War: American forces routed British and German troops at the Battle of Bennington in Walloomsac, New York.
American Revolutionary War: The Americans led by General John Stark rout British and Brunswick troops under Friedrich Baum at the Battle of Bennington in Walloomsac, New York.
American Revolutionary War: Battle of Camden: The British defeat the Americans near Camden, South Carolina.

main.desc: 1780 battle of the American Revolutionary War

events.text: Maximilien Robespierre presents the petition of the Commune of Paris to the Legislative Assembly, which demanded the formation of a revolutionary tribunal.
French Revolution: A levée en masse is decreed by the National Convention.
War of 1812: American General William Hull surrenders Fort Detroit without a fight to the British Army.
Around 15 people were killed and 400 to 700 others injured when cavalry charged into a crowd demanding the reform of parliamentary representation in Manchester, England.

main.desc: Soldiers or warriors fighting from horseback

events.text: Peterloo Massacre: Seventeen people die and over 600 are injured in cavalry charges at a public meeting at St. Peter's Field, Manchester, England.

main.desc: 1819 massacre by government troops in Manchester

events.text: Daaga and two other African soldiers in the British Army's 1st West India Regiment were executed for their role in the St. Joseph Mutiny in Trinidad.
Three African soldiers in the 1st West India Regiment – Daaga, Edward Coffin and Maurice Ogston – are executed for their role in the St. Joseph Mutiny in the British colony of Trinidad.

main.desc: Infantry units of the British Army

events.text: U.S. President John Tyler vetoes a bill which called for the re-establishment of the Second Bank of the United States. Enraged Whig Party members riot outside the White House in the most violent demonstration on White House grounds in U.S. history.

links.t: Second Bank of the United States

events.text: Governor-general of the Philippines Narciso Claveria signs a decree to reform the country's calendar by skipping Tuesday, December 31, as a solution to anomalies that had existed since Ferdinand Magellan's arrival in 1521.

main.desc: Spanish Governor-General of the Philippines from 1844 to 1849

events.text: U.S. President James Buchanan inaugurates the new transatlantic telegraph cable by exchanging greetings with Queen Victoria of the United Kingdom. However, a weak signal forces a shutdown of the service in a few weeks.

main.desc: President of the United States from 1857 to 1861

events.text: The Grand Duchy of Tuscany formally deposes the exiled House of Lorraine.
The Dominican Restoration War begins when Gregorio Luperón raises the Dominican flag in Santo Domingo after Spain had recolonized the country.

main.desc: 1863–1865 war between the Dominican Republic and Spain

events.text: Battle of Acosta Ñu: A Paraguayan battalion largely made up of children is massacred by the Brazilian Army during the Paraguayan War.
Franco-Prussian War: The Battle of Mars-la-Tour is fought, resulting in a Prussian victory.
Richard Wagner's Siegfried, the penultimate opera in his Ring cycle, is premiered at the Bayreuth Festspielhaus.
San Sebastian Church (pictured), an all-iron church in Manila, was officially consecrated.

main.desc: Roman Catholic church in Manila, Philippines

events.text: The Basilica of San Sebastian, Manila, the first all-steel church in Asia, is officially inaugurated and blessed.

main.desc: Roman Catholic church in Manila, Philippines

events.text: A group including George Carmack and Skookum Jim Mason discovered gold  near Dawson City, Canada, setting off the Klondike Gold Rush.

main.desc: Prospector who discovered gold which led to the Klondike Gold Rush

events.text: Skookum Jim Mason, George Carmack and Dawson Charlie discover gold in a tributary of the Klondike River in Canada, setting off the Klondike Gold Rush.
Second Boer War: A 10,000-strong column of soldiers led by Lord Kitchener broke a 13-day siege of a small garrison.

The Battle of Elands River during the Second Boer War ends after a 13-day siege is lifted by the British. The battle had begun when a force of between 2,000 and 3,000 Boers had surrounded a force of 500 Australians, Rhodesians, Canadians and British soldiers at a supply dump at Brakfontein Drift.

main.desc: Battle of the Second Boer War

events.text: An earthquake registering approximately 8.2 Mw struck Valparaíso, Chile, killing 3,882 people.
The 8.2 Mw Valparaíso earthquake hits central Chile, killing 3,882 people.
Tōhoku Imperial University of Japan (modern day Tohoku University) becomes the first university in Japan to admit female students.
Completion of the Royal Navy battlecruiser HMS Queen Mary.

main.desc: Naval warfare force of the United Kingdom

events.text: German admiral Wilhelm Souchon hands over the two warships under his command to the Ottomans and becomes commander of the Turkish navy, leading later to the entry of the Ottoman Empire in World War I.
The Migratory Bird Treaty between Canada and the United States is signed.

main.desc: 1916 treaty between Canada and the United States

events.text: The Battle of Lake Baikal is fought between the Czechoslovak Legion and the Red Army.

main.desc: 1918 battle of the Russian Civil War

events.text: The Battle of Radzymin, one of the bloodiest and most intense battles of the Polish–Soviet War, concluded with a Polish victory.
In the United Kingdom, the Blind Persons Act received royal assent.

main.desc: Act of the Parliament of the United Kingdom

events.text: Ray Chapman of the Cleveland Indians was hit by a pitch and died the following day, becoming the only Major League Baseball player to die directly as a result of injuries sustained during a game.

Ray Chapman of the Cleveland Indians is hit on the head by a fastball thrown by Carl Mays of the New York Yankees. Next day, Chapman will become the second player to die from injuries sustained in a Major League Baseball game.
The congress of the Communist Party of Bukhara opens. The congress would call for armed revolution.

main.desc: Ruling political party of the Bukharan SSR (1920–24)

events.text: Polish–Soviet War: The Battle of Radzymin concludes; the Soviet Red Army is forced to turn away from Warsaw.
The United Kingdom gives the name "Ross Dependency" to part of its claimed Antarctic territory and makes the Governor-General of the Dominion of New Zealand its administrator.

main.desc: New Zealand's territorial claim in Antarctica

events.text: The Dole Air Race begins from Oakland, California, to Honolulu, Hawaii, during which six out of the eight participating planes crash or disappear.
A long-running dispute between Muslims and Jews over access to the Western Wall in Jerusalem escalated into a week-long period of violent riots throughout Palestine.

main.desc: Holy site of Judaism in Jerusalem

events.text: The 1929 Palestine riots break out in Mandatory Palestine between Palestinian Arabs and Jews and continue until the end of the month. In total, 133 Jews and 116 Arabs are killed.
The first color sound cartoon, Fiddlesticks, is released by Ub Iwerks.
The first British Empire Games are opened in Hamilton, Ontario, by the Governor General of Canada, the Viscount Willingdon.

main.desc: Multi-sport event involving athletes from the Commonwealth of Nations

events.text: Christie Pits riot takes place in Toronto, Ontario.
The Holocaust: During the deportation of Jews from Slovakia, President Jozef Tiso gave a speech describing Jews as "parasites" and "the eternal enemy".

main.desc: Genocide of European Jews by Nazi Germany

links.t: List of Holocaust transports from Slovakia

events.text: World War II: US Navy L-class blimp L-8 drifts in from the Pacific and eventually crashes in Daly City, California. The two-man crew cannot be found.
World War II: 317 Greek civilians are murdered by soldiers of the German 1st Mountain Division in the village of Kommeno, Greece.

main.desc: Nazi war crime committed in Greece

events.text: First flight of a jet with forward-swept wings, the Junkers Ju 287.
The Stanley Internment Camp in Hong Kong was liberated following the announcement of the surrender of Japan in World War II.

main.desc: Civilian internment camp in Hong Kong

events.text: The National Representatives' Congress, the precursor of the current National Assembly of Vietnam, convenes in Sơn Dương.
Widespread riots between Hindus and Muslims took place in Calcutta following the All-India Muslim League's call for an independent Pakistan.
Mass riots in Kolkata begin; more than 4,000 people would be killed in 72 hours.
The All Hyderabad Trade Union Congress is founded in Secunderabad.

main.desc: Trade union in the Indian state of Hyderabad

events.text: The first issue of Sports Illustrated is published.
Cyprus gains its independence from the United Kingdom.

main.desc: Island country in the Mediterranean Sea

events.text: Joseph Kittinger parachutes from a balloon over New Mexico, United States, at 102,800 feet (31,300 m), setting three records that held until 2012: High-altitude jump, free fall, and highest speed by a human without an aircraft.
The English rock band the Beatles fired their drummer Pete Best, replacing him with Ringo Starr (pictured).
Vietnam War: A coup d'état replaces Dương Văn Minh with General Nguyễn Khánh as President of South Vietnam. A new constitution is established with aid from the U.S. Embassy.

Vietnam War: The House Un-American Activities Committee begins investigations of Americans who have aided the Viet Cong. The committee intends to introduce legislation making these activities illegal. Anti-war demonstrators disrupt the meeting and 50 people are arrested.
In an unsuccessful coup d'état attempt, the Royal Moroccan Air Force fires upon Hassan II of Morocco's plane while he is traveling back to Rabat.

Australian Prime Minister Gough Whitlam symbolically hands over land to the Gurindji people after the eight-year Wave Hill walk-off, a landmark event in the history of Indigenous land rights in Australia, commemorated in a 1991 song by Paul Kelly and an annual celebration.

main.desc: Prime Minister of Australia from 1972 to 1975

events.text: American singer and actor Elvis Presley (pictured), often referred to as the "King of Rock and Roll", was found dead in his home in Memphis, Tennessee.
Typhoon Wayne formed over the South China Sea, going on to become one of the longest-lived tropical cyclones in the north-western Pacific, lasting 21 days.
A Sudan Airways Fokker F27 Friendship is shot down near Malakal in present day South Sudan, killing 60.
Northwest Airlines Flight 255, a McDonnell Douglas MD-82, crashes after takeoff in Detroit, Michigan, killing 154 of the 155 on board, plus two people on the ground.
A solar particle event affects computers at the Toronto Stock Exchange, forcing a halt to trading.
Indian Airlines Flight 257, a Boeing 737-200, crashes during approach to Imphal Airport, killing all 69 people on board.
West Caribbean Airways Flight 708, a McDonnell Douglas MD-82, crashes in Machiques, Venezuela, killing all 160 people on board.
The Trump International Hotel and Tower in Chicago is topped off at 1,389 feet (423 m), at the time becoming the world's highest residence above ground-level.
